messages:
devon: heads-up — i sketched a migration playbook for moving prefix residency to the epoch-based flow (residency-v2). want to validate the operator steps and rollback triggers before we schedule a canary.

maria: nice. can you paste the high level phases?

devon: sure — phases: discovery, canary (single region, low-traffic), ramp (more tenants + autoscale), soak, cutover. each phase has safety gates: ops checks + automated metric thresholds.

raj: what are the invariants we need to assert during canary?

maria: minimal list: no read-after-write regressions, no prefix ownership duplicates, eviction counts for canary tenants <= baseline + 5%, request p99 latency delta < 15ms, KV-miss-rate doesn't spike. also ensure tombstone/compaction behavior unchanged.

sasha: add: ensure sequence tokens don't regress for long-lived cursors. i hit a subtle cursor reset in last experiment.

devon: good call. playbook includes per-tenant smoke tests (read/write sequences, cursor resume) and an automated "ownership-scan" that verifies each prefix has at most one active residency owner.

maria: what about prefill? we have to avoid cold starts that trigger mass prefill and cause OOMs.

devon: plan: disable reactive prefill during the initial canary, rely on on-demand fetch + small controlled prefill window. ops command to toggle:

```
# toggle reactive prefill for a tenant
rictl tenant-config set $TENANT prefill.enabled=false
```

raj: how will handoff happen when we flip tenant to v2? is it a migration or dual-run?

devon: dual-run for safety. both residency engines run in read-path. writes for v2-tenants go through v2. Read-path prefers v2 ownership if present, otherwise v1 fallback. we have a deterministic tie-breaker (epoch higher wins). handback uses a graceful drain: source owner sets handoff intent, destination pulls KV snapshot of resident keys, then the source revokes after checkpoint.

maria: need a guard for in-flight writes during handoff — double-apply window?

sasha: we should use write-sequencing: during handoff, a short write-forward period where writes are accepted by both sides but sequenced by a monotonic op-id. That reduces chance of lost updates.

devon: agreed — handoff steps in playbook:
1) mark tenant as migrating (feature-flag)
2) wait for quiet window (short, configurable)
3) snapshot resident prefixes
4) enable v2 ownership + prefill (controlled)
5) redirect new writes to v2 with op-id pinning
6) verify parity checksums for hot prefixes
7) flip read-preference to v2
8) revoke v1 leases once checks pass

raj: what parity checks? hashes per-prefix?

devon: per-prefix small rolling hash + item counts + top-N hotkeys. not full CRC for every key (too expensive), but enough to catch divergence.

maria: what metrics and dashboards do we need for the rollout page?

devon: list in playbook: residency-owner-count, ownership-duplicates, per-tenant-evictions, prefix-prefill-rate, prefix-mismatch-count, long-cursor-reset-rate, kv-read-latency-p99, kv-write-errors. each metric has an alert threshold configured for canary and ramp.

ops-bot: deploy: canary/residency-v2 enabled for cluster-03 by @devon at 2024-11-07T15:12:03Z

sasha: small ops note — make sure compact/GC jobs are rate-limited during canary, compaction can amplify small discrepancies into noisy deletes.

devon: added a step: throttle GC and compaction to 20% of normal during phases 1-3.

maria: rollback plan? what are hard triggers to stop and revert?

devon: rollback triggers: ownership-duplicates > 0 for 5m, prefix-mismatch-count > 2 for 10m, kv-write-errors > 0.1% sustained 5m, p99 latency delta > 50ms 5m. rollback action: flip feature-flag to v1-only, run a restore conciliator that rehydrates any missing prefixes to v1 owner, unthrottle compaction.

raj: how long until safe to decommission v1 for a tenant?

devon: minimum 72h of healthy metrics + 2 successful full parity scans separated by 12h. then plan for an async decommission job which verifies no active cursors and cleans up v1-residency metadata.

maria: canary tenant candidates? pick low-traffic but representative ones (mix of small and mid-sized keyspace). add a tenant that uses long-lived cursors.

sasha: i'll prepare a short chaos schedule to inject node restarts and network partitions during soak to ensure handoff tolerates jitter.

devon: final checklist for on-call before starting canary: ops toggle commands, rollback commands, parity-run script, metric dashboard link, runbook owner, pager rotation for next 72h. i'll paste commands in the playbook doc.

maria: thanks — looks solid. once you drop the doc link i'll spin up the dashboard and add alerts. :+1:

devon: dropping doc in #eng-docs in 10m. planning canary for next tuesday, pending ✓ from SRE.

ops-bot: reminder: deploy window reserved 2024-11-12 02:00-05:00 UTC (automated infra maintenance)

raj: one last edge-case — leases that were force-revoked by operator in last 24h. those prefixes may lack tombstone metadata. add a reconcile step that rebuilds tombstone markers before flip.

devon: good catch. added preflip reconcile to playbook (rebuild missing tombstones + run tiny rehydrate).

sasha: ok from me. i'll coordinate chaos tests and the canary tenant list.

maria: assigning runbook owner to devon, SRE sign-off requested.

devon: thanks — i'll iterate on the doc and ping for a final review.
